samples.summary: getWrapAffinity fix does not reach blocks inside NESTED table cells — they still always answer 'backward'
samples.evidence: getWrapAffinity now delegates to getVisualLineRange, whose cell branch resolves the cell layout via `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId)` (text-editor.ts:4058). For a block inside a table nested in another table, `cellInfo.tableBlockId` is the INNER table, which is not a top-level block of the layout, so `tableLb` is undefined; the code then falls through to `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === pos.blockId)` (4091), which also misses a cell-inner block, and returns `[0, 0]` → getWrapAffinity yields 'backward' for every offset > 0. So the exact defect the diff's comment claims to fix ('walking getLayout().blocks directly never matched a block inside a table cell') persists one nesting level down, even though resolveOffsetInNestedTable in the same diff now produces 'forward' affinities for those cells — hit-test and post-insertion affinity disagree inside nested tables.

samples.summary: getWrapAffinity now routes every keystroke through getVisualLineRange's unguarded `rows[rowIndex].cells[colIndex]` dereference (possible TypeError)
samples.evidence: getWrapAffinity (4140-4143) is called after every insertText/composition commit (lines 333, 559, 587, 647, 698, 744, 3646, 3701, 3773, 5242). It now enters the cell branch of getVisualLineRange, which does `const cell = tableBlock.tableData!.rows[cellInfo.rowIndex].cells[cellInfo.colIndex];` (4063) with no optional chaining, using indices from `blockParentMap` — a map that is only rebuilt inside recomputeLayout (editor.ts:1306-1313), i.e. on the next animation frame. If the doc's table shrank since the last layout (row/column delete queued via markDirty, layout not yet recomputed), `rows[rowIndex]` is undefined and the expression throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')` inside the input handler. Before this change getWrapAffinity never touched table layout, so this dereference was only reachable from Home/End/vertical-move.

samples.summary: Empty cell layout gives targetLineIdx = -1, so isFirstLineOfBlock is false and offset 0 is reported as 'forward'
samples.evidence: `let targetLineIdx = cell.lines.length - 1;` (4715) leaves -1 when a cell layout has no lines; the new closure `hitTestLineAffinity(o, lineStartOffset, targetLineIdx === blockStartLine)` (4812) then compares -1 to blockStartLine (0), so isFirstLineOfBlock is false and the fallthrough return at 4876 (`offset` = 0 = lineStartOffset) yields 'forward' for the very first character position of the cell block — an affinity that claims a preceding visual line that does not exist. Same pattern in resolveOffsetInNestedTable: `let lineIdx = cellLayout.lines.length - 1` (4960) with `lineIdx === blockStartLine` at 5008.

samples.summary: The 'past end of line' return still hardcodes 'backward' while every other return now goes through affinityForOffset
samples.evidence: After introducing `affinityForOffset` (line 117-118), the final return (194-198) keeps `lineAffinity: 'backward'`. For a continuation line whose char count is 0 (layout.ts:578-596 documents that a trailing `\n` produces an empty trailing visual line) `endOffset === charsBeforeLine`, so this path contradicts the rule the new helper encodes for the identical offset reached via the other branches. Behaviour is unchanged from before the diff, but the inconsistency is now explicit.

samples.summary: getWrapAffinity computes affinity against a layout that has not yet been re-laid-out for the text just inserted
samples.evidence: Callers such as handleInput do `this.docInsertText(...)`, `this.markDirty(blockId)` and then `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, this.getWrapAffinity(newPos))` before `requestRender()` (text-editor.ts:728-745). markDirty only queues an id (editor.ts:1316-1321); `layout`/`headerLayout` are replaced only inside recomputeLayout during the rAF render. So getWrapAffinity compares the POST-insertion `newPos.offset` against PRE-insertion visual line starts, and can answer 'forward'/'backward' for a wrap boundary that the insertion moved. The behaviour predates the diff, but the new doc comment presents the helper as reading the authoritative active layout, which it does not.

verdict.reason: The finding checks out in the repository. text-editor.ts:4063 dereferences `tableBlock.tableData!.rows[cellInfo.rowIndex].cells[cellInfo.colIndex]` with no optional chaining; the only preceding guards (4059 `tableLb?.layoutTable`, 4061 `layoutCell && !layoutCell.merged`) read the cached layout, so they pass whenever layout and blockParentMap are stale together while the doc is fresh — exactly the divergence that crashes. getWrapAffinity (4140-4142) does now route through getVisualLineRange, and indices come from getActiveLayout().blockParentMap (3134-3138), which is only rebuilt in recomputeLayout (editor.ts:1306-1313) via render() (editor.ts:1917-1920). A concrete reachable stale window exists: docs-view.tsx:373 calls updateCompositionStartPosition (→ editor.ts:3621 → text-editor.ts:333 getWrapAffinity) before editor.render() at docs-view.tsx:380, so a remote row/column delete that shifts the caret's cell (block still resolvable via document.ts:226-237 fallback walk, but stale row/col indices) reaches 4063 with an out-of-range index. handleInput (744) and insertText (559) also call getWrapAffinity before requestRender with no try/catch, unlike the arrow path which is explicitly wrapped for this very hazard (text-editor.ts:2462-2469, whose comment names "Stale blockParentMap data (e.g. table rows removed by remote edit)") because moveLeft/moveRight do the same unguarded deref (3920, 3968). Missing-guard crash in an input handler is in the Correctness lane and blocking; no guard makes it unreachable.
